title: US Approves Treatment for Severe High Blood Pressure
titleZh: 美国批准用于治疗严重高血压的新疗法
credits: Lauran Neergaard wrote this story for The Associated Press. Andrew Smith adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Michael Garrity had dangerously high blood pressure for many years.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·加リティは長年にわたり危険なレベルの高血圧だった。

sentences.en: And the medicines that doctors gave him could not control it.
sentences.zh: 医師が彼に処方した薬ではそれを抑えられなかった。

sentences.en: But a new treatment targeting some nerves on his kidneys has helped the 62-year-old Garrity have normal blood pressure for the first time in years.
sentences.zh: しかし、腎臓にある一部の神経を狙った新しい治療法により、62歳の加リティは数年ぶりに正常な血圧を取り戻した。

sentences.en: When some nerves from the kidneys send more signals than is normal, dangerously high blood pressure can result.
sentences.zh: 腎臓からの神経が通常より多くの信号を送ると、危険なレベルの高血圧を引き起こすことがある。

sentences.en: The new treatment uses ultrasound, or high frequency sound waves, to reduce the signals the nerves send.
sentences.zh: 新しい治療法は、超音波、つまり高周波の音波を用いて、神経が送る信号を減少させる。

sentences.en: “My blood pressure would spike and I’d run out of breath and feel tired, and that doesn’t happen anymore,” said Garrity, who lives in the American state of Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 「私の血圧は急上昇し、息切れを起こし、疲れを感じていましたが、もうそんなことはありません」と、マサチューセッツ州に住む加リティは語った。

sentences.en: Garrity still takes medicine but at lower amounts.
sentences.zh: 加リティは今も薬を飲んでいるが、量は減っている。

sentences.en: He said he is very happy with the results of his treatment.
sentences.zh: 彼は治療結果に大変満足していると言う。

sentences.en: About half of U.S. adults have high blood pressure.
sentences.zh: アメリカの成人の約半分が高血圧である。

sentences.en: It increases the risk for heart attacks, strokes, kidney failure, and possibly dementia.
sentences.zh: それは心臓発作、脳卒中、腎不全、そして認知症のリスクを高める。

sentences.en: Many people do not know they have high blood pressure until something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 多くの人は何かが起きるまで、自分が高血圧であることを知らない。

sentences.en: “Know your blood pressure, know the numbers,” said Dr. Randy Zusman of Massachusetts General Hospital.
sentences.zh: 「自分の血圧を知り、数値を知りなさい」と、マサチューセッツ総合病院のランディ・ズスマン医師は言う。

sentences.en: He treats difficult cases.
sentences.zh: 彼は難治性の症例を治療している。

sentences.en: He also said people who think they are healthy should still have their blood pressure measured once a year or more.
sentences.zh: また、健康だと考えている人も、少なくとも年に一度は血圧を測定すべきだと述べた。

sentences.en: Only a small percentage of people with high blood pressure control the condition well.
sentences.zh: 高血圧の人のうち、状態をうまくコントロールできているのはごく一部である。

sentences.en: That might mean there is a need for new treatments.
sentences.zh: それは、新しい治療法が必要かもしれないことを意味する。

sentences.en: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the new ultrasound treatment about a year ago.
sentences.zh: アメリカ食品医薬品局（FDA）は約1年前に新しい超音波治療法を承認した。

sentences.en: Some hospitals are offering the treatment, but only for patients who might be likely to have good results.
sentences.zh: 一部の病院はこの治療法を提供しているが、効果が見込める患者に限っている。

sentences.en: Blood pressure is measured using two values.
sentences.zh: 血圧は2つの数値で測定される。

sentences.en: One value is called “systolic” pressure.
sentences.zh: 一方の数値は「収縮期」血圧と呼ばれる。

sentences.en: It is the force blood puts on the walls of arteries as it is pumped out of the heart.
sentences.zh: 血压是血液被心脏泵出时对动脉壁施加的力。

sentences.en: The second value is called “diastolic” pressure.
sentences.zh: 第二个数值被称为'舒张压'。

sentences.en: That number measures pressure in blood vessels between heartbeats.
sentences.zh: 这个数字衡量的是两次心跳之间血管内的压力。

sentences.en: The Associated Press reports that normal blood pressure is less than 120 over 80.
sentences.zh: 美联社报道说，正常血压低于120/80。

sentences.en: However, blood pressure naturally changes throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 然而，血压在一天中会自然变化。

sentences.en: It is higher when a person is physically active or experiences tension.
sentences.zh: 当人进行体力活动或感到紧张时，血压会升高。

sentences.en: But when it stays higher than, for example, 130 over 80 or higher, it might mean the heart is working too hard.
sentences.zh: 但当它持续高于例如130/80或更高时，可能意味着心脏负担过重。

sentences.en: Instead of drugs, doctors advise lifestyle changes as the first step to reduce blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 与药物相比，医生建议将生活方式的调整作为降低血压的第一步。

sentences.en: Changes can include losing weight, getting regular exercise, eating more fruits and vegetables, limiting salt and alcohol, and taking steps to deal with tension, or stress, in a healthy way.
sentences.zh: 这些改变可以包括减轻体重、规律锻炼、多吃果蔬、限制盐分和酒精摄入，以及以健康的方式应对紧张或压力。

sentences.en: However, if blood pressure reaches 140 over 90, taking medicine becomes necessary.
sentences.zh: 然而，当血压达到140/90时，服药就变得必要了。

sentences.en: Zusman said most patients need two or three drugs, sometimes more, along with healthier living.
sentences.zh: 苏斯曼说，大多数患者需要服用两三种药物，有时更多，同时配合更健康的生活方式。

sentences.en: The high blood pressure Garrity has struggled with resists treatment with drugs.
sentences.zh: 加列蒂长期困扰的高血压对药物治疗产生了抵抗。

sentences.en: He tried taking four to six drugs as well as eating healthy food and exercising.
sentences.zh: 他尝试过服用四到六种药物，同时健康饮食和锻炼。

sentences.en: Still, his blood pressure regularly reached 150 over 100 or higher.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他的血压仍经常达到150/100或更高。

sentences.en: Dr. Joseph Garasic is a heart specialist at Massachusetts General Hospital.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·加拉斯基博士是马萨诸塞通义医院的一名心脏专家。

sentences.en: He performed Garrity’s operation.
sentences.zh: 他实施了加列蒂的手术。

sentences.en: He said doctors pass a small tube through blood vessels to reach the kidneys.
sentences.zh: 他说，医生会通过血管插入一根细管到达肾脏。

sentences.en: Then they direct ultrasound through kidney arteries targeting the nerves.
sentences.zh: 然后他们通过肾脏动脉将超声波对准神经。

sentences.en: The operation takes about one hour.
sentences.zh: 手术大约需要一个小时。

sentences.en: The treatment is not a cure, and it does not help all patients.
sentences.zh: 这种治疗并非根治，也不能帮助所有患者。

sentences.en: But Garasic said several studies show on average an eight to 10-point drop in blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 但加拉斯里克表示，多项研究表明，血压平均下降8到10个点。

sentences.en: This small decrease can still help some patients.
sentences.zh: 这种小幅下降仍对部分患者有所帮助。

sentences.en: Others, like Garrity, see bigger drops.
sentences.zh: 而其他人，比如加里蒂，血压下降幅度更大。

sentences.en: This can help reduce the number of medications patients must take.
sentences.zh: 这有助于减少患者需要服用的药物数量。

sentences.en: Studies connected to the new ultrasound treatment have only lasted a few years.
sentences.zh: 与新型超声治疗相关的研究只持续了几年时间。

sentences.en: That means doctors do not yet know if the nerves will grow back.
sentences.zh: 这意味着医生还不知道这些神经是否会重新长出来。

sentences.en: The American Heart Association says people with high blood pressure and their doctors should have “thoughtful and informed discussions” to decide who might be the right patients to try the treatment.
sentences.zh: 美国心脏协会表示，高血压患者及其医生应当进行'深思熟虑且有充分依据的讨论'，以决定谁可能是适合尝试这种治疗的患者。

sentences.en: I’m Andrew Smith.
sentences.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。
